beats: title: The story of this class: three families in the colonies of Texas, from the fall of 1835 to the spring of 1836.
arrival: Three families came to new land in the colonies, near San Felipe de Austin, Columbia and Mina.
call: Riders brought word that soldiers had come for the cannon at Gonzales. From one family men rode to join the volunteers. Two families kept to their farms.
fight: The fight at Concepción: Jonas Flashwright.
fight: The Grass Fight: Jonas Flashwright.
fight: The storming of Béxar: Jonas Flashwright.
fight: The Alamo: Jonas Flashwright and Nathan Flashwright. Jonas Flashwright was killed there. Nathan Flashwright was killed there.
news: Word that the Alamo had fallen reached Joel's family on March 14, and the Flashwright family only on March 14, one day later.
flight: In March word came that the Mexican army was coming, and every family was told to leave for the east. Three families loaded their wagons and set out.
sickness: Sickness came to two families on the road and in the camps.
burned: Mexican foragers burned the farm of the Flashwright family. The family did not know it for days.
fight: San Jacinto: Zadok Harrowgate and Josiah Harrowgate.
home: After San Jacinto the families went home: two families to houses still standing, and one family to ashes. Two of the class's people did not come home from the war.
closing: Five of the class's people went to the war. Every family has its own story, and each of you will now see yours, on your own screen.

hh-1: home: The family came home. The house was ashes, burned by Mexican foragers. They had carried a hoe, a felling axe, the bedding and the iron pot all the way home. They found one cow and 5 hogs again.
rebuild: In the days after, they raked out the ashes and began again: the first logs of a new house went up where the old one had stood.
burial: The family gathered under the trees by the house to remember Nathan and Jonas, and set up two wooden markers in their memory.
count: Mary sat down at the table to count what the family had left: 206 reales in coin, and one head of cattle and five hogs on the range. The farm was ashes: there was nothing left of it to sell.
hh-2: home: The family came home. The house was still standing. Josiah was already there, home since April 28. Zadok was already there, home since April 28.
count: Josiah sat down at the table to count what the family had left: 12 reales in coin.

sale: A land agent from Columbia came out and bought the farm, the land, the round-log cabin, 30 acres of cleared field, fenced and the well, for 75 reales. With the coin in the house, the family had 87 reales.
